_comment: Feature 006 — the committed source of the in-app client changelog. Ingested at agent boot and via POST /admin/content/reingest. Each entry upserts by `slug` (idempotent); entries the seed no longer lists are PRUNED on ingest — seed-owned rows only, including pre-slug legacy rows — so a reset leaves exactly this file. An operator's live Admin -> Updates edit wins and is preserved; an unreadable/empty file never prunes. Client-facing register: keep it tester-friendly, no dev detail.

entries.title: Comparisons answer only when they actually compare
entries.body: When you ask Sparky to compare two protocols, it now answers only when the reply actually names both options and does not open with a flat refusal. When SparkPoint has verified material for every option, the answer includes its sources; if material is missing for any one of them, the comparison is still shown but without a partial "Sources" block. If the reply is just a refusal, Sparky replaces it with its honest structural summary. Behind the scenes, the agent records why a comparison was replaced or left uncited — counts and reasons only, never your message or the answer text. Nothing about reviewing, signing or your funds changes.

entries.title: Comparisons now come with real, grounded answers
entries.body: When you ask Sparky to compare two protocols, it now looks up each one by name instead of searching the whole sentence once. So "Is Morpho safer than Aave?" gets the Morpho and Aave material it needs, rather than a general release note. If SparkPoint has verified material for only one side, Sparky says that plainly and still explains the well-known structural differences for the other side — without inventing rates or figures, giving allocation advice or suggesting a transaction. A comparison that Sparky cannot ground is no longer shown with a "Sources" block, so a non-answer can never look like a sourced answer. Nothing about reviewing, signing or your funds changes.

entries.title: Comparison questions get a real answer instead of a retry error
entries.body: Asking Sparky to compare two options — for example "Is Morpho safer than Aave?" — could end in a "try again" error even after the answer had started to appear. That is fixed: Sparky now finishes a comparison with a useful, honest answer (how the risks differ, how the yield is produced and what the fees look like), or says plainly when it cannot verify a detail, instead of reporting a model problem that did not happen. A genuine provider outage still shows the normal retry message. Nothing about reviewing, signing or your funds changes.

entries.title: Sparky's answers now stream as they are written — and comparisons get a real answer
entries.body: Sparky's replies now start appearing in the chat as they are written instead of arriving all at once when the answer is finished. A behind-the-scenes gateway was holding every word until the end; it now passes each word through immediately, so a normal answer starts painting in a fraction of a second while the rest is still being written. The complete, checked answer still replaces what you saw, is the only version saved to your history, and nothing about reviewing or signing changes. Comparative questions also get a proper answer now: ask "Is Morpho safer than Aave?" or "Compare that with just keeping it in Aave" and Sparky compares the risks, how the yield is produced and the fees from its grounded product knowledge — instead of returning a generic empty-wallet message, and without preparing any transaction.

entries.title: Sparky tells a price question from an earnings estimate
entries.body: Ask for the current price of a coin and Sparky still answers with a live reference figure, its source and the time it was read. Ask what an amount could earn over time — for example "how much is 10k USDC in 1 year?" or "what would $500 in ETH earn in 6 months?" — and it now treats that as an estimate request instead of quoting a single spot price. If a live price cannot be fetched, Sparky says so instead of guessing.

entries.title: Behind the scenes: cleaner bookkeeping when an answer fails
entries.body: When an AI answer fails because the provider is briefly unavailable, that question still does not count against your daily allowance. We fixed an internal check that wrongly reported those refunds as failed. Nothing changes in how you use Sparky.

entries.title: Sparky reads the whole question before answering
entries.body: A short, simple question about what is in your wallet is still answered instantly. Anything that asks for advice, describes a hypothetical, mentions an action or amount, or adds another request now goes through Sparky's full understanding step instead of being mistaken for that simple check. So questions like "How should I fund my wallet?" or "What happens if I lose my wallet?" get a real answer about what you asked, not a bare balance snapshot.

entries.title: Sparky gets a nightly quality check
entries.body: Every night we now run Sparky through more than 70 real questions, including tricky and adversarial ones, and check that its answers stay accurate, grounded and safe. Changes to how Sparky thinks are checked against the same set before they ship, so fixes stay fixed.

entries.title: Sparky now types its answers as it thinks
entries.body: Sparky now types its answers as it thinks, so replies start appearing in about a second instead of after the whole answer is ready. Questions about your portfolio, what's new, fees and the live vault rate are now answered without waiting on a second AI step, and the reply still arrives complete and checked before it is saved to your history. If a reply has to be replaced for safety, the replacement is what you see and what is kept. Nothing about signing or your funds changes: Sparky still only prepares moves for you to review and sign.

entries.title: Sparky answers the awkward questions instead of hitting a dead end
entries.body: Ask Sparky how to earn with an empty wallet and you now get the curated vault options with their current net APY and as-of date, a plain-language estimate when you give an amount and a time frame (clearly labelled as an estimate, not a promise), and a real comparison with simply keeping your money in Aave. It also remembers the amount from earlier in the conversation, so "what if I only put half?" works. Asking for the safest vault now prepares a move you can review and sign instead of just describing it, "withdraw everything" prepares the full withdrawal (or says there is nothing to withdraw), and a simple "do it" follows the last move Sparky proposed. Swaps into assets we don't support yet — like native BTC, SOL or NEAR — now say so honestly and point you at what is live today, and requests to send funds to a third party or ignore Sparky's safety rules get a clear refusal. Sparky never moves funds; you always review and sign.

entries.title: A degraded answer no longer costs a question
entries.body: Sometimes the AI provider is briefly unavailable and Sparky falls back to a short "try again" message instead of a real answer. That turn used to still count against your daily chat allowance. Now, if a reply degrades like that and no real answer was produced, the question is returned to you. Successful answers still cost one question, and closing the chat mid-reply never changes your allowance.

entries.title: Behind the scenes: security refresh
entries.body: We patched the web framework and the validation libraries against newly published vulnerabilities. Nothing changes in how the app looks or works — your wallet, your keys, and how you sign stay exactly the same.

entries.title: Sparky chat is back — and a failed answer no longer costs a question
entries.body: Free chat is working again after the model provider retired the models Sparky was using. Sparky now has extra models on different providers behind the scenes, so if one is busy or unavailable it tries another before giving up. If a turn still fails because the AI provider is unavailable, it no longer counts against your daily chat, recommendations, or onboarding allowance — you keep the question. Successful turns work exactly as before.

entries.title: Sparky now answers price questions — and every APY shows how fresh it is
entries.body: Ask Sparky "what is the price of ETH today?" and you now get a live USD reference quote for ETH (plus BTC, SOL and NEAR for context), with the source and the time it was checked in UTC. Stablecoins are shown at about $1, and if a stable moves outside its usual band Sparky says so instead of hiding it. Prices move constantly, so the answer carries a reminder that a quote is not financial advice; if the price feed can't be reached, Sparky says it can't fetch one rather than guessing. SRK still has no dollar price, because there is no oracle and we won't invent one. Every stored vault APY now shows its as-of date too, and if the figure is more than about two days old Sparky tells you how old it is and points you to the Vault page for the live rate. Sparky's product knowledge was also expanded so questions about Morpho vs Aave, how APY and net APY work, slippage and the 0.20% swap fee, NEAR Intents (planned for the November build), self-custody and signing, daily question limits, and mandates get grounded answers.

entries.title: A calmer app: no pop-up blocking you, and helpful dead ends
entries.body: The What's New note no longer covers the app while you are trying to use it — it is now a small panel you can dismiss, and it only greets you once per release. The Strategies tab is hidden while there are no strategies to show, rather than leading to an empty page. On phones the header is tidier, and the trust banner can be dismissed for good. The vault page now refreshes every minute instead of constantly, so it uses much less data and battery. In chat, a slow answer now says Sparky is taking longer than usual, and a failed or rate-limited turn explains when your allowance resets and points you to the Vault, Swap and changelog, which keep working without Sparky. You can now rate a chat answer with a thumbs up or down; the rating is stored so it can improve answers. Signing in also no longer waits forever if the assistant is briefly unreachable — you continue straight to the app.

entries.title: Sparky's knowledge updates ride out busy moments
entries.body: When the AI provider briefly rate-limits, the system that keeps Sparky's product knowledge up to date now waits and retries a few times instead of skipping that update. Nothing changes in how you use the app — answers just stay grounded in the latest docs more reliably.

entries.title: Sparky runs on a new model lineup — and reads your product docs more sharply
entries.body: Sparky's chat now runs on a newer generation of models on both the Beta and the Alpha: quicker free models for everyday questions and a stronger premium model for deeper ones. Its knowledge search also moved to a new embedding system, and we re-indexed everything it reads — the product docs, the changelog, and the tips — so answers about how SparkPoint works stay grounded in the current text. The daily research Sparky does on its own (checking vaults and writing its findings) now runs on the premium model too, on both environments. Nothing about your wallet, your keys, or how you sign changed.

entries.title: The beta is open — bring a wallet
entries.body: No more invite list: connect a wallet and sign the free message to prove it's yours, and you're in. Chat with Sparky, see your portfolio, swap ETH and USDG, and browse the vault board. SparkPoint never holds your funds — you sign every transaction yourself, and you can withdraw any time.

entries.title: Sparky Brokers now has its own stop on the landing page
entries.body: Scroll just past the hero and you'll meet the Brokers: 10,000 memberships whose two-pixel gold frame is the proof of activation. A short preview shows the unactivated → activated look, and the OpenSea link takes you straight to the collection.

entries.title: The access application's tab title no longer stutters
entries.body: Small copy fix: the browser tab on the access application read “Apply for beta access — Sparky — Sparky”. It now says it once, and the same fix applies to the alpha build's wording.

entries.title: The site now calls itself what it is — Beta
entries.body: The landing page, the access application, and a few app notes still said “alpha” even though you are using the Beta. They now all read the site's real stage, so the beta says Beta and the alpha/testnet build still says Alpha. Nothing about your access or funds changed — this is wording catching up with the product you're already using.

entries.title: Safety answers that never wait on a model
entries.body: Questions about custody — “how do you keep my funds safe?”, “can you withdraw my funds?” — are now answered directly from the system's own guarantees, so they stay available even when the AI provider is busy. The chat's swap suggestion also names the pair you're actually swapping (ETH and USDG on this network).

entries.title: Sparky handles busy moments better
entries.body: When the model provider is briefly rate-limiting, Sparky now waits and retries a few more times instead of giving up, so a busy moment is less likely to end in “something went wrong”. Asking what a vault is paying is also answered straight from the same stored figure the Vault board shows.

entries.title: Asking Sparky what vaults are available now works
entries.body: Asking “what are the vaults available right now?” used to get a generic “no strategy clears your guardrails” reply. Sparky now lists the curated vaults from the same board the Vault page shows, names the current pick, and links the board. The withdrawal receipt also shows the amount you actually withdrew instead of $0.00, and the wallet answer names the token you really hold (USDG on this network).

entries.title: The portfolio's Withdraw action is keyboard-friendly
entries.body: A small accessibility fix: the Withdraw control on a held position is now a real button you can tab to, not just a click target.

entries.title: Withdraw straight from a vault card
entries.body: If you hold a curated vault, its card on the Vault page now shows your position and a Withdraw action that takes you to the withdraw screen with that vault selected. Your Portfolio row links there too. Share amounts on the deposit and withdraw screens are also shown at the right scale, and the withdraw preview names the token you'll actually receive.

entries.title: The deposit acknowledgement tells the truth
entries.body: The confirmation's acknowledgement used to claim it was using your “full idle balance” and called the token USDC — even for a small deposit of USDG. It now names the real asset and the real share of your idle balance, and what stays in your wallet.

entries.title: Deposits into curated vaults can be signed again
entries.body: The confirm screen was waiting on a check that only applies to SparkPoint's own vault, so the sign button never appeared for a curated vault on the beta. It now verifies the deposit directly on-chain and tells you plainly that the policy check doesn't apply to third-party vaults. The confirm copy also names the token you're actually depositing (USDG), and your wallet list now shows the tokens we know for the network.

entries.title: Revenue: every token, in its real units
Behind the scenes: steadier history indexing
entries.body: A fix in how the background indexer tracks its progress across networks — one chain's activity can no longer stop another chain's deposit and withdrawal history from updating.

entries.title: Your beta positions now show profit and loss
entries.body: Once you hold a curated vault on the beta, Portfolio shows its cost basis and unrealized profit or loss, and the value chart starts drawing from your real deposits and withdrawals. Before the first deposit it stays honestly blank — no placeholder numbers.

entries.title: Sparky now sees your beta portfolio
entries.body: When you ask about your portfolio or where to put your funds, Sparky reads the same balances the Portfolio page shows — your idle USDG and any curated vault positions you hold — so its suggestions start from what you actually have, not from a blank slate.

entries.title: Your portfolio now shows your real funds
entries.body: On the beta, Portfolio shows what your wallet actually holds: your USDG balance (at $1 par), your ETH, and any curated vault positions you hold — all read live on-chain. Before you deposit, your idle balance sits right there with a one-tap “Put it to work”. You can also add any token by address to see it in your wallet list.

entries.title: The beta reads in one voice
entries.body: The landing page, onboarding, portfolio, premium and automation screens, and the chat suggestion chips now describe only what's live in the beta — curated vaults, swaps, and your wallet. Nothing you read points at something you can't use today.

entries.title: The beta now speaks only to what's live
entries.body: A copy pass across the app: the vault picker, deposit and withdraw notices, strategies, fees and portfolio now describe only the live curated-vault program, so every label and notice matches something you can actually use today.

entries.title: Updates now reach open tabs reliably
entries.body: We fixed the last piece of the update-refresh flow: the build identifier the app uses to detect a new release was being generated twice with different values, so an open tab could think it was permanently out of date. It is now stable per release, and the app reloads cleanly onto a new build when one ships.

entries.title: Deposit screen fixes, clearer button labels, and fresh builds
entries.body:
The Deposit screen now opens correctly for the wrapped curated vaults on Robinhood Chain (it previously showed a 'not part of the beta yet' notice), and the button now names the token — 'Deposit USDG' — instead of internal wording. The Portfolio note now points to the live curated vaults.

We also fixed app updates not showing up until a hard refresh: new builds now reach an open tab and the update banner can reload onto them cleanly.

entries.title: Real token logos in the swap and vault pages
entries.body: USDG, ETH and the Robinhood stock tokens now show their real logos in the swap picker, the vault cards and your portfolio — no more plain letter circles. The art is bundled with the app (no third-party calls), and logos stay decorative: the verified badge is still what tells you a token is the right one.

entries.title: You can deposit into the wrapped vaults now
entries.body:
The Vault page's recommended vault and every live vault card now open a working deposit flow: the app resolves the SparkPoint wrapper, shows the wrapper's own fee disclosure, and signs the deposit against it. The card also shows the stored curator-scan net APY, labelled as a stored figure, and withdrawals are never gated.

Under the hood this wires the app to the new V3 wrapper fleet — one wrapper per vault, deployed on-chain and verified.

entries.title: Vault page: full-colour pick card and honest wrapper status
entries.body: The recommended-vault card now wears SparkPoint's full brand gradient, and a vault whose wrapper is deployed no longer claims otherwise — it says plainly that in-app deposits for it are coming shortly.

entries.title: The Vault page is card-first — and shows only vaults you can deposit into
entries.body:
Sparky's recommended vault now leads the page in a full-width feature card, and every live vault sits below as a card with its net APY, TVL, withdrawable liquidity and a 30-day trend chart — no more table. Scroll and more cards load in.

We also tightened what's public: only vaults whose SparkPoint wrapper is actually deployed appear here, so every card is depositable today. Vaults still being screened or wrapped are handled in the admin panel and are never shown as 'coming soon'.

entries.title: Under the hood: one clean vault-admission queue
entries.body: The vault admission flow now has a single queue. The old wrapper-request path was retired after the new admission queue went live — the AI can admit a curated vault under the public cooling-off window, and the operator keeps the instant lane. Nothing changes for you: deposits, withdrawals and fees are untouched.

entries.title: Curated vaults: wrapping now follows a public cooling-off window
entries.body:
When a curated vault gets its SparkPoint wrapper, the AI can now admit it on its own — but the wrapper is not deployable until a public cooling-off window elapses (24 hours by default, configurable between 1 hour and 7 days). The operator can admit and deploy a vault immediately, release a cooling-off entry early, or cancel a pending one, and one wrapper per vault is enforced on-chain.

The Trust Center now spells this out, including that upgrades still wait out the 72-hour timelock and withdrawals are never gated.

entries.title: Under the hood: a safer path to automatic vault wrapping
entries.body:
We are upgrading how a curated vault gets its SparkPoint wrapper. Under the new on-chain model, the AI can admit an approved vault on its own but must wait out a public cooling-off window before it can wrap it (24 hours by default, operator-configurable between 1 hour and 7 days); the operator keeps an instant lane to add, release, or cancel a wrapper, and one wrapper per vault is enforced on-chain.

This groundwork is being rolled out now, so the Vault page will say plainly when a wrapper is live. Nothing changes about fees or exits: performance-only above your high-water mark, and withdrawals are never gated.

entries.title: Curated vaults: clearer wrapper fees and upgrades
entries.body:
Wrapped curated vaults now explain their upgrade model up front: every wrapper upgrade must wait out a public 72-hour timelock, a separate multisig can cancel it, and nothing — not a pause, not an upgrade, not SparkPoint — can stop you from withdrawing.

The Vault page also keeps its promise to say exactly where a fee applies: a vault shows the SparkPoint wrapper deposit path only after the wrapper has actually been deployed, and a wrapper is never shown before then. Fees stay performance-only: gains above your high-water mark, never a deposit, a withdrawal, or a losing position.

entries.title: The Vault page is now just the curated board
entries.body:
We removed the “SparkPoint’s own vault” card. SparkPoint is not launching its own vault on this network — the plan is to find strong vaults that already exist here, wrap them in SparkPoint’s own upgradeable wrapper, and bring them to the Vault page for you to use.

When the first vault is onboarded it will appear on the board by itself; until then the page says honestly that there is nothing to show. Deposits and withdrawals always stay in your own wallet.

entries.title: Under the hood: upgradeable curated-vault wrappers
entries.body:
We built the system that lets SparkPoint wrap a curated vault in its own upgradeable wrapper — so fees on gains stay future-proof and fixes can reach every wrapper at once.

Nothing changes on this network yet: there is still no curated vault live here, so there is nothing to deposit. When one goes live, the Vault page will show it with the full fee disclosure, and you will always sign from your own wallet.

entries.title: Sparky now hunts for the best vaults for you
Swapping: more tokens, fewer taps
A cleaner beta: honest labels, tidier pages, less clutter
SparkPoint beta is live on Robinhood Chain
